title: Bidirectional Dijkstra in Barcelona: Scale Routing ⚡
description: Watch Bidirectional Dijkstra race two frontiers—one from start, one from destination—until they meet. In a dense grid like Barcelona’s Eixample, the speedup shows up instantly in the number of explored nodes.
ig_caption:
Bidirectional Dijkstra: How Modern Route Planners Scale — inside high-scale navigation engines, Bidirectional Dijkstra visualised ⚡

In this Barcelona (Eixample) map, we run TWO Dijkstra searches: one forward from the start and one backward from the goal.
✅ Each side expands the lowest-cost frontier (priority queue)
✅ Expansion stops when the frontiers meet and we can prove the best path
✅ Result: fewer visited nodes → faster shortest path at scale

Takeaway: Same shortest-path guarantee, but you reduce work by shrinking the search space from both ends.

Debate: Should production route planners prefer bidirectional search—or go all-in on heuristics like A* (or contraction hierarchies)?
